subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs gain a supported model/provider override contract, and if so should it be `payload.model`, a top-level job override, or a dedicated `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes public cron schema, session/provider precedence, persistence, and upgrade behavior; automation should not pick that API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Extend systemEvent payload.model
options.body: Add `payload.model` to `systemEvent` cron payloads with explicit provider/model validation and direct heartbeat/session routing proof, matching the existing `agentTurn` override style.

options.title: Add job-level override fields
options.body: Introduce a top-level model/provider override that can apply across cron payload kinds, at the cost of a broader contract and migration/docs surface.

options.title: Keep main-session systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document isolated `agentTurn` as the supported per-job model path and leave main-session system events tied to the target session's model state.

recommendation.title: Extend systemEvent payload.model
recommendation.body: Add `payload.model` to `systemEvent` cron payloads with explicit provider/model validation and direct heartbeat/session routing proof, matching the existing `agentTurn` override style.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime and model-routing history makes this the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
